title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: A 38-Hour Week, Fortnight, and the UK Average Salary Comparison
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using a 38-hour week, 52 weeks, and fortnightly calculations. Includes tax, super, and a UK average salary comparison.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top and tax deducted using 2026–27 rates.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the base rate for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries and occupations, as published by the Fair Work Ombudsman in pay guides. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum wage, making it $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. It is not deducted from your hourly rate or salary; your employer adds it separately. For example, on a $26.44 hourly rate, super is $3.17 per hour extra.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Pay to Annual Salary: The 38-Hour Week and Fortnight

Understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential for budgeting and comparing job offers. In Australia, the standard full-time working week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Commission. The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a 38-hour week, this becomes: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for estimating your total earnings.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Weekly pay is hourly rate × 38. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, weekly pay is $1,004.90, and fortnightly pay is $2,009.80. This can help you align with your pay cycle and manage cash flow.

## National Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. This rate applies to adult employees who are award/agreement free. Most workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that provides higher minimum rates. You can find the correct pay guide for your industry on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum wage, bringing the casual rate to $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave. When using our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) calculator, enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box to add 25% automatically. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

## Tax and Superannuation

Your gross annual pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:
- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Most residents also pay a Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low incomes). The tax-free threshold is included. For a precise estimate, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator.

Superannuation Guarantee requires your employer to contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit. For example, on a $26.44 hourly rate, your employer adds $3.17 per hour to your super fund.

## Comparing to the UK Average Salary

When evaluating job offers, you might wonder how Australian pay compares internationally. The **uk average salary** is a common benchmark, but it is typically quoted in pounds sterling and based on different working hours and tax systems. While the UK average full-time salary is around £35,000–£40,000 per year (depending on the source), Australian full-time adult average weekly earnings were $2,083.70 per week as of May 2026, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352.40 for a 52-week year. This is significantly higher than the UK average when converted to Australian dollars, but cost of living and tax rates differ. Our focus here is on Australian pay calculations, but understanding the **uk average salary** can help you contextualise your earnings if you are considering work abroad or comparing multinational offers.

## Practical Example

Suppose you are offered $30 per hour as a permanent full-time employee. Your annual gross pay would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. Fortnightly gross pay is $30 × 38 × 2 = $2,280. After tax (using 2026–27 rates and Medicare), your take-home pay would be approximately $47,000 per year, depending on your circumstances. Your employer would also contribute $7,113.60 to super (12% of $59,280).

For casual employees at the same base rate, the hourly rate becomes $37.50 (including 25% loading), giving annual gross of $74,100 and fortnightly gross of $2,850.

## Important Notes

This conversion assumes a consistent 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It does not account for salary sacrifice, HELP repayments, or the Medicare levy surcharge. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax calculations use the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold and the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare (as the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed). Always consult a qualified accountant or use official tools for binding advice.

For more details, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.
